subject: history
title: Trade, and why the cities crumbled

nodes: Villages around the cities grow grain
Traded for goods made in the cities
props.label: Trade, p.32

scenes.narration: The grains probably came from the villages around the cities. The villages may have traded grain for goods produced in the cities. Roads and the Indus river system were used for trade.

nodes: A dockyard at Lothal: overseas trade with western Asia
props.label: By sea, p.32

scenes.narration: Ornaments made in the Indus Valley have been found in Mesopotamia. A dockyard found at Lothal suggests overseas trade with western Asia.

nodes: Natural and environmental disasters: earthquakes, floods, drought
Falling soil quality; desertification from deforestation
People move away; the cities crumble
props.label: After 2000 BCE, p.32

scenes.narration: The civilisation declined suddenly after 2000 BCE. The exact causes remain a mystery. Disasters, poor soil from deforestation, or the authority losing control may have made people move away, and the cities crumbled.
